defects.fix_lead: Either add an option/explanation acknowledging all three caps (position-size, concentration, sector) are breached, or restructure the mandate/numbers so single-stock concentration is genuinely not implicated (e.g. make the concentration cap higher than 14.5%, or clarify concentration is measured differently from position size). Also point related_lesson at a position-sizing/concentration lesson instead of stop-loss basics.

defects.issue: Internal math in the quoted trader ticket doesn't reconcile: risk per share is $412.40-$405.80=$6.60 (1.6% of entry price). At a stated 1.5% NAV loss cap, sizing to fully use that cap would require committing ~93.75% of NAV to this single position (shares = NAV*1.5%/6.60, position value = NAV*0.9375) — not the stated 3.2% of NAV. As written, sizing to only 3.2% of NAV would risk just ~0.05% of NAV, nowhere near the claimed 1.5% loss cap being used. Doesn't change the keyed answer (still clearly the Trader speaking) but the quoted numbers are not mutually consistent.
defects.fix_lead: Either widen the stop distance or shrink the position-size percentage so 'sizes to X% of NAV' and 'mandate-permitted 1.5% loss cap' actually reconcile (e.g. a $6.60 stop at 1.5% loss cap implies a much smaller position size than 3.2% only if NAV or stop distance is scaled differently).

defects.fix_lead: Reword explanation to say capex is stepping up from its current (lower) level to RM12B, which is what will turn the currently-positive RM3.2B FCF negative — don't call the RM3.2B 'operating FCF' pre-capex.

defects.fix_lead: Adjust share count/price so notional lands at or under exactly 6.00% of NAV (e.g. 17.9 shares worth, or reduce price/shares slightly) so only the stop-loss rule is breached.

defects.issue: Says share price is 'determined continuously by the highest bid and lowest ask' — actually the traded share price is the last executed trade price (which occurs when a bid and ask cross/match), not simply the current best-bid/best-ask values; conflates quoted spread with traded price.
defects.fix_lead: Reword to: price is set by the most recent trade, which occurs when a buyer's bid and seller's ask match; the current bid/ask bracket where the next trade is likely to occur.

defects.issue: Definition says musharakah partners 'share profit and loss in a pre-agreed ratio' — under the standard Sharia rule (and AAOIFI-consistent majority fiqh position, confirmed via web search), profit follows the pre-agreed ratio but loss must be shared strictly in proportion to each partner's capital contribution, not any separately agreed ratio; conflating the two misstates a defining feature of the contract.
defects.fix_lead: Rewrite: 'partners share profit in a pre-agreed ratio, while loss is shared strictly in proportion to capital contribution' — mirror the correct asymmetric rule already stated correctly in the mudarabah entry.

Directly relevant since the entry says 'AMI's screening logic follows' these numbers.
defects.fix_lead: Correct to 30%/30%/5% for AAOIFI, or if AMI's backend genuinely uses 33%/33%/5%, re-attribute those defaults to the correct standard (e.g., S&P/MSCI/DJIM-style) rather than labeling them AAOIFI's.

defects.fix_lead: Align the stated caps and standard-name with whichever is actually implemented in `sharia_screen`: either 30%/30%/5% attributed to AAOIFI, or keep 33%/33%/5% but stop calling it 'AAOIFI-style.'
